name: The man who refused the prophetic command
charge: Refusing to smite the prophet when commanded in the word of the Lord
summary: One of the sons of the prophets told his neighbour, by the word of the Lord, to strike him, and the neighbour refused. The prophet told him that because he had not obeyed the voice of the Lord a lion would kill him as soon as he left, and a lion met him and killed him (1 Kings 20:35-36). The blow was needed for the sign that would bring Ahab to pronounce his own sentence for sparing Ben-hadad.
offenseFull: The man who gave the command was one of the sons of the prophets (1 Kings 20:35). The sons of the prophets were schools of instruction that go back to the spirit the Lord took from Moses and put on the seventy elders (Numbers 11:25). Samuel stood as the appointed head over a company of them (1 Samuel 19:20), and there were schools at Ramah, at Jericho and at Bethel, where Elijah and Elisha often went and where the people came on Sabbaths and new moons for public lessons in the law of Moses. So when this man spoke to his neighbour in the word of the Lord, it came with the weight of the Lord’s appointed teachers, not as a private whim.

The command belonged to a prophetic act aimed at the king. Ahab had just sent Ben-hadad away on a covenant, though the Lord had marked him for destruction (1 Kings 20:34, 42). The prophet needed to stand before the king wounded and disguised with ashes, as a soldier who had lost a prisoner put in his charge on pain of his own life, so that the king would judge the case and pass sentence on himself (1 Kings 20:37-40). The neighbour was not asked to decide whether the message should go forward, only to do his part in it. His refusal may have looked like kindness toward a prophet, but the prophet named it for what it was: he had not obeyed the voice of the Lord (1 Kings 20:36).
judgmentFull: The sentence was spoken at once: as soon as he left, a lion would kill him; and as soon as he left, a lion found him and killed him (1 Kings 20:36). The judgment fell before the message ever reached the king. The prophet found another man and told him to strike him, and that man struck and wounded him (1 Kings 20:37). The work went on without the one who refused. The prophet waited for the king by the road with ashes on his face and told his story; the king ruled that the soldier had decided his own sentence; and when the ashes came off, the king saw that he was one of the prophets and heard that his own life would go for Ben-hadad’s life, and his people for Ben-hadad’s people (1 Kings 20:38-42). He went home to Samaria sullen and angry (1 Kings 20:43), crying again over a just judgment because he would not obey the voice of the Lord.

The chapter holds two refusals of a received command: the neighbour who would not strike, and the king who would not destroy. The same thing had happened to the man of God out of Judah, who turned back to eat at Bethel against the word given him, and a lion met him on the road and killed him (1 Kings 13:21-24). Under that dispensation disobedience to the mouth of the Most High carried the penalty of death. The study notes draw the lesson for us: we are to do as it is written, that we may be justified and our life not be taken from us for rebellion against the Lord.

text.text: And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said unto his neighbour in the word of the Lord, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man refused to smite him.

Then said he unto him, Because thou hast not obeyed the voice of the Lord, behold, as soon as thou art departed from me, a lion shall slay thee. And as soon as he was departed from him, a lion found him, and slew him.
And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said unto his neighbour in the word of the Lord, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man refused to smite him.

And the Lord came down in a cloud, and spake unto him, and took of the spirit that was upon him, and gave it unto the seventy elders: and it came to pass, that, when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease.

And Saul sent messengers to take David: and when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing as appointed over them, the Spirit of God was upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied.

And Ben–hadad said unto him, The cities, which my father took from thy father, I will restore; and thou shalt make streets for thee in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria. Then said Ahab, I will send thee away with this covenant. So he made a covenant with him, and sent him away.

And he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Because thou hast let go out of thy hand a man whom I appointed to utter destruction, therefore thy life shall go for his life, and thy people for his people.
Then he found another man, and said, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man smote him, so that in smiting he wounded him.
So the prophet departed, and waited for the king by the way, and disguised himself with ashes upon his face.

And as the king passed by, he cried unto the king: and he said, Thy servant went out into the midst of the battle; and, behold, a man turned aside, and brought a man unto me, and said, Keep this man: if by any means he be missing, then shall thy life be for his life, or else thou shalt pay a talent of silver.
And as thy servant was busy here and there, he was gone. And the king of Israel said unto him, So shall thy judgment be; thyself hast decided it.

Then said he unto him, Because thou hast not obeyed the voice of the Lord, behold, as soon as thou art departed from me, a lion shall slay thee. And as soon as he was departed from him, a lion found him, and slew him.
Then he found another man, and said, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man smote him, so that in smiting he wounded him.
So the prophet departed, and waited for the king by the way, and disguised himself with ashes upon his face.

And as the king passed by, he cried unto the king: and he said, Thy servant went out into the midst of the battle; and, behold, a man turned aside, and brought a man unto me, and said, Keep this man: if by any means he be missing, then shall thy life be for his life, or else thou shalt pay a talent of silver.
And as thy servant was busy here and there, he was gone. And the king of Israel said unto him, So shall thy judgment be; thyself hast decided it.
And he hasted, and took the ashes away from his face; and the king of Israel discerned him that he was of the prophets.

And he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Because thou hast let go out of thy hand a man whom I appointed to utter destruction, therefore thy life shall go for his life, and thy people for his people.
And the king of Israel went to his house heavy and displeased, and came to Samaria.

And he cried unto the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Forasmuch as thou hast disobeyed the mouth of the Lord, and hast not kept the commandment which the Lord thy God commanded thee,

But camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk water in the place, of the which the Lord did say to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no water; thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers.
And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that he saddled for him the ass, to wit, for the prophet whom he had brought back.
And when he was gone, a lion met him by the way, and slew him: and his carcase was cast in the way, and the ass stood by it, the lion also stood by the carcase.
And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said unto his neighbour in the word of the Lord, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man refused to smite him.

Then said he unto him, Because thou hast not obeyed the voice of the Lord, behold, as soon as thou art departed from me, a lion shall slay thee. And as soon as he was departed from him, a lion found him, and slew him.
Then he found another man, and said, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man smote him, so that in smiting he wounded him.
So the prophet departed, and waited for the king by the way, and disguised himself with ashes upon his face.

And as the king passed by, he cried unto the king: and he said, Thy servant went out into the midst of the battle; and, behold, a man turned aside, and brought a man unto me, and said, Keep this man: if by any means he be missing, then shall thy life be for his life, or else thou shalt pay a talent of silver.
And as thy servant was busy here and there, he was gone. And the king of Israel said unto him, So shall thy judgment be; thyself hast decided it.
And he hasted, and took the ashes away from his face; and the king of Israel discerned him that he was of the prophets.

And he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Because thou hast let go out of thy hand a man whom I appointed to utter destruction, therefore thy life shall go for his life, and thy people for his people.
And the king of Israel went to his house heavy and displeased, and came to Samaria.
